title: Separated smooth Gaussian Bobkov bound
statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $[0,1]$, and let $D(x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous linear functional at each $x$. Suppose $D(x)$ is the derivative of $f$ at $x$, the map $x\mapsto D(x)$ is globally Lipschitz with some constant $C\ge0$ in operator norm, and $\|D(x)\|\le M$ for every $x$, for some real $M$. Then
\[
U\!\left(\int f\,d\gamma_n\right)\le \int U(f(x))\,d\gamma_n(x)+\int\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(D(x)e_i)^2}\,d\gamma_n(x),
\]
where $e_i$ are the coordinate unit vectors, $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure, and $U$ is the Gaussian profile that equals the Gaussian density at the Gaussian quantile on $(0,1)$ and zero elsewhere.
hypotheses_covered: $D(x)$ is a continuous linear functional for each $x$
$D(x)$ is the derivative of $f$ at $x$ for every $x$
The map $x\mapsto D(x)$ is globally Lipschitz with constant $C\ge0$
There is a real $M$ with $\|D(x)\|\le M$ for every $x$
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,1]$ be differentiable with derivative family $D(z)$, globally $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm for the maximum norm, where $C\ge0$. Write $|D(z)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n(D(z)e_i)^2}$. If also $\|D(z)\|\le M$ for every $z$, for some $M\in\mathbb R$, then $\overline I(\int f\,d\gamma_n)\le\int\overline I(f)\,d\gamma_n+\int|D(z)|_2\,d\gamma_n(z)$.
